calls.body: The Golden Knights have been one of the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Canucks the worst. story.head: Stone ties Marchessault for the Golden Knights’ points record
paras: The Canucks snapped a seven-game losing streak. The first period was a wild one. Elias Pettersson (#40) and Linus Karlsson scored four and a half minutes apart early in the period to put the Canucks up 2-0. Victor Olofsson got the Golden Knights on the board on the power play less than four minutes later. Filip Chytil pushed the lead to 3-1 just over four minutes later, and he scored his second of the night shorthanded early in the second to make it 4-1. Braeden Bowman cut Vancouver’s lead to 4-2 midway through the period. Mark Stone made it 4-3 on the power play early in the third, but they got no closer. Drew O'Connor made it 5-3 for the Canucks 24 seconds later, and Karlsson struck again into the empty net with a little over two minutes left.

The Golden Knights had a little more of the play, but the Canucks made their chances count. Leevi Meriläinen, who gave up five goals against the Rangers in his last start, made 34 saves for the Canucks, and Carter Hart allowed five goals on 26 shots.

A scrum at the final horn sent five players to the box, with five misconducts. The Canucks improved to 4-17-1, still last in the NHL, while the Golden Knights dropped to 13-6-3, second in the Pacific.

items.text: Mark Stone tied Jonathan Marchessault for first on the Golden Knights’ all-time scoring list, with 417 points.
The Golden Knights’ six-game point streak is over.
Tomáš Hertl has a point in seven straight games.
Filip Chytil scored his first two goals of the season, his first since Oct 16, 2025 (16 games played since).
